name: Dusty cerise
lede: Dusty cerise is a deep, warm pink, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Kobai-iro, "red plum colored," named for a flowering tree rather than the cherry its English name suggests.

sections.title: The color of red plum blossom
sections.body:
Kobai-iro (紅梅色) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for "red plum colored," after the red-flowering plum, not the cherry fruit that the English word cerise, French for cherry, points to here [1]. The page gives no further history for the name beyond that literal meaning, and it is undocumented in the sources consulted here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor on file is [[mayflower]], 3.0 units off [2]; [[carmine-red]] sits 4.0 off, almost the same pink from an entirely different source.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, 0.03 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 4 [3]. That makes it rarer than 77 percent of the named colors in our library, a genuinely scarce match [3]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications; a color this saturated and specific rarely survives the aging and varnishing that most of our archive has been through [3].
